A direct check on a location-translation family of Gaussian wavepackets confirms this: with $\pi=0$ and $u=-\hbar(x-\theta)/(2m\sigma^{2})$, one has $\operatorname{Cov}(u,u)=\hbar^{2}/(4m^{2}\sigma^{2})$. Multiplying by $C=4m^{2}/x^{2}$ yields $1/\sigma^{2}$, which equals both the optimal classical Fisher information and the pure-state QFI $F_{Q}=4[\langle\partial\psi|\partial\psi\rangle-|\langle\psi|\partial\psi\rangle|^{2}]$. The un-suppressed factor $m^{2}/x^{2}$ would instead give only $1/(4\sigma^{2})$, i.e. the standard FS metric, which is not the SLD-based quantum Fisher metric.

\boxed{4m^2/x^2}
